title: Postdoctoral/Research Fellowship at NUS Asia Research Institute 2026: S$6,000–S$6,500 Monthly Salary for Ageing and Migration Research
summary: The Asia Research Institute (ARI) at the National University of Singapore (NUS) is inviting applications for a full-time Postdoctoral/Research Fellow position focused on ageing, migration, social networks, healthcare, eldercare, digital inclusion, and long-term integration among foreign-born older adults in Singapore. The position offers an opportunity for an early-career researcher with a PhD in the social sciences or humanities to join a four-year research project funded by Singapore’s Social Sciences Research Council (SSRC) under its Thematic Grant programme. The successful candidate will become part of an interdisciplinary research team examining how foreign-born older adults build and access formal and informal support systems locally and across borders. The fellowship is particularly relevant to researchers specialising in social geography, sociology, anthropology, migration studies, ageing studies, qualitative research, social networks, healthcare, eldercare, or related areas . The appointment is initially for one year , with the possibility of renewal into a second year. The successful candidate is expected to begin work at NUS in October 2026 and no later than December 2026 . Opportunity Overview Opportunity: Postdoctoral/Research Fellowship Institution: Asia Research Institute, National University of Singapore Research Cluster: Migration and Mobilities Cluster Research Theme: Ageing and Migration Project: Ageing Futures and Resource Environments of Foreign-born Singapore Residents Location: Kent Ridge Campus, Singapore Employment Type: Full-time Initial Appointment: One year Renewal: Possibility of renewal into the second year Monthly Salary: S$6,000–S$6,500, depending on experience Expected Start Date: October 2026, and no later than December 2026 Application Deadline: 14 August 2026 Req ID: 33777 About the Asia Research Institute at NUS The Asia Research Institute (ARI) is a research institute within the National University of Singapore that brings together scholars working on major social, cultural, economic and political issues affecting Asia. For this fellowship, the successful researcher will be hosted within ARI s Migration and Mobilities Cluster . The researcher will work under the leadership of Prof Elaine Ho , who serves as the Principal Investigator, alongside an interdisciplinary team of Co-Investigators. This creates an opportunity for the successful applicant to work in a research environment where migration and ageing are examined from multiple disciplinary perspectives. About the Ageing and Migration Research Project The fellowship is connected to a four-year research project titled “Ageing Futures and Resource Environments of Foreign-born Singapore Residents.” The project is supported through the Social Sciences Research Council Singapore Thematic Grant programme and focuses on the relationship between two major life-course transitions: ageing and migration . Ageing and migration can both involve significant changes in people s social relationships, access to resources, identities, communities and opportunities. However, the two processes have often been investigated separately. This research project seeks to bridge that gap. What are “resource environments”? A major concept within the project is the idea of resource environments . In this context, resource environments refer to the formal and informal sources of support that older adults develop and use. These resources may exist within Singapore or extend across national borders. They can include: Family and kinship networks Friends and community networks Healthcare services Eldercare services Social support systems Community organisations Digital communication networks Transnational relationships Informal care arrangements Formal institutional support Opportunities for productive ageing The project is particularly interested in how foreign-born older adults navigate these resources and how their access to different forms of support influences their experiences of ageing in Singapore. Who Will the Research Focus On? The successful fellow will primarily conduct qualitative research involving foreign-born Singapore residents aged 55 years and above . The research participants will originate from different countries in Asia. The project will also compare foreign-born older adults with local-born older adults . Through this comparison, researchers will explore how different resource environments influence: Belonging Social participation Access to opportunities Healthcare experiences Eldercare arrangements Social networks Digital inclusion Long-term integration Experiences of ageing Key Research Areas The project brings together several interconnected areas of research. 1. Ageing The research examines how people experience later life and how ageing interacts with social, economic and community environments. 2. Migration Migration is central to the project because it can influence access to family networks, social services, healthcare, community relationships and other forms of support. 3. Social Networks The study will investigate how older adults develop and maintain relationships that provide emotional, practical and other forms of support. 4. Healthcare Healthcare access and experiences are important components of the research, particularly in understanding the resources available to older foreign-born residents. 5. Eldercare The project will explore formal and informal systems of care and how older adults navigate these systems. 6. Digital Connectivity Digital technologies can enable older adults to maintain relationships across borders and access information and services. The project therefore considers digital connectivity as part of people s resource environments. 7. Productive Ageing The research will also examine opportunities and experiences associated with productive ageing, including participation and contribution during later life. 8. Integration and Belonging The project seeks to understand how resource environments affect older adults sense of belonging, participation and long-term integration. Responsibilities of the Postdoctoral/Research Fellow The successful candidate will primarily be responsible for conducting qualitative research in Singapore . This will involve engaging with foreign-born Singapore residents aged 55 and above and gathering qualitative data through methods such as interviews and observations. The researcher will also work closely with colleagues from different academic disciplines because the broader project uses a mixed-methods and interdisciplinary approach . Major responsibilities are expected to include: Conducting Qualitative Fieldwork The fellow will undertake community-based research involving foreign-born older adults. This may involve: Conducting interviews Undertaking observations Engaging with research participants Building relationships within communities Collecting qualitative research data Analysing interview and observational findings Participating in Interdisciplinary Research Because the project brings together researchers from different disciplinary backgrounds, the successful applicant will be expected to collaborate with researchers who may use different theoretical approaches and research methodologies. The ability to communicate effectively across disciplines will therefore be important. Research Analysis The fellow will contribute to analysing research findings and connecting qualitative evidence with the wider mixed-methods research programme. Academic Writing The successful candidate will participate in research writing connected to the project. This may include contributing to: Research papers Journal articles Conference papers Research reports Other scholarly publications Non-Academic Research Dissemination The position also includes opportunities to contribute to communicating research findings to non-academic audiences. This could involve translating research findings into accessible materials for stakeholders, policymakers, community organisations and other audiences. Professional Development Opportunities The fellowship provides several opportunities for the successful researcher to strengthen their academic profile and research career. Present Research at Conferences The fellow will have opportunities to present research findings at both international and domestic conferences . This can help researchers build professional networks, receive feedback on their work and increase the visibility of their research. Publish in High-Impact Journals The successful applicant will have the opportunity to participate in joint authorship of publications in high-impact peer-reviewed journals . This can be particularly valuable for researchers seeking to establish or strengthen their academic publication record after completing their PhD. Participate in Workshops and Seminars The fellow may participate in and help organise: Project meetings Workshops Seminars Academic discussions Research activities Grant Development The position also provides exposure to grant funding applications , giving the successful candidate an opportunity to develop experience in research funding and project development. Participate in Cluster Projects Beyond the specific ageing and migration project, the researcher will be able to participate in current activities within the ARI Migration and Mobilities Cluster. Eligibility and Academic Requirements Applicants are expected to meet several academic and professional requirements. PhD Requirement Applicants should hold a PhD degree , or be awaiting formal conferment of their PhD. The PhD should be in a relevant field within the Social Sciences and Humanities . The advertisement particularly identifies the following fields as preferred: Social Geography Sociology Anthropology Migration Studies Researchers from closely related disciplines may also be relevant where their research background aligns strongly with the project s themes. Research Interest Applicants should be able to demonstrate a clear research interest in themes relevant to the project. Relevant areas may include ageing, migration, mobility, social networks, healthcare, eldercare, digital inclusion, integration, community studies or related subjects. Qualitative Research Skills Strong qualitative research skills are an important requirement. Applicants should be able to demonstrate experience or capability in conducting qualitative research, particularly research involving communities and human participants. Experience with mixed-methods research will be considered an advantage. Language Skills Because the researcher will conduct community-based fieldwork, conversational proficiency in one or more languages central to the project is required. These include: Hindi Tamil Bengali Tagalog Bahasa Indonesian Vietnamese Applicants who can communicate conversationally in one or more of these languages may therefore be particularly well positioned for the fieldwork component of the fellowship. Publication Potential Applicants should demonstrate the potential to develop a strong publication record, particularly through publications in high-impact peer-reviewed journals . Applicants with previous academic publications should clearly demonstrate these achievements in their CV and application materials. Communication Skills The successful candidate should have a high level of competence in both written and spoken communication. Strong academic writing ability is particularly important because the position involves research publications, dissemination and collaboration with researchers from different disciplines. Interpersonal and Teamwork Skills The fellow will work with: Academic researchers Co-Investigators Community members Non-academic stakeholders Other research staff Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate effectively are therefore essential. Salary and Employment Benefits The position offers an all-inclusive fixed monthly salary of S$6,000 to S$6,500 , depending on the successful applicant s experience. The stated monthly amount includes stipends intended to cover: Housing expenses Living expenses Applicants should therefore consider the all-inclusive nature of the salary when evaluating the financial terms of the appointment. Travel Assistance for Overseas Applicants Successful applicants coming from overseas will receive travel assistance . This can be particularly useful for international researchers relocating to Singapore for the appointment. CPF Benefits Singapore citizens and permanent residents are eligible for Central Provident Fund benefits . Taxation Salary and benefits-in-kind are subject to taxation according to applicable Singapore tax laws. International applicants should therefore consider the applicable tax implications when assessing the overall compensation package. Research and Conference Support The position provides support for project-related research fieldwork and conference attendance , subject to approval. This means the successful researcher may receive institutional/project support for eligible activities directly related to the research project. The opportunity to attend conferences can also contribute to professional development and academic networking. Expected Participation in ARI Activities Research staff at ARI are expected to actively participate in the institute s research environment. This includes attending activities such as: Research seminars Conferences Academic events ARI social events Other relevant research activities Applicants should therefore be comfortable working in a collaborative research environment rather than operating exclusively as an independent researcher. Appointment Duration and Start Date The initial appointment is for one year . However, there is a possibility of renewal into the second year. The successful applicant is expected to commence duties at NUS in October 2026 , and in any event no later than December 2026 . Applicants should therefore be prepared to take up the appointment within this timeframe. Application Requirements Applicants must combine all required application documents into one PDF document . The combined PDF should then be attached under the CV column when submitting the application. The required documents are: 1. Curriculum Vitae The CV should provide a clear overview of the applicant s: Academic qualifications Research experience Publications Research methods Relevant professional experience Conference participation Language skills Other achievements relevant to the position Given the highly specialised nature of the role, applicants should ensure that their CV clearly demonstrates their connection to ageing, migration, qualitative research or related project themes. 2. Cover Letter The cover letter must be no more than 800 words . It should explain: The applicant s previous research experience Their research expertise Their aptitude for the project Why their background aligns with the research themes Relevant methodological experience Their ability to contribute to the interdisciplinary research team Applicants should use the cover letter to directly connect their previous research experience with the requirements of the fellowship. 3. Academic Transcripts Applicants must provide their relevant academic transcripts as part of the combined PDF. 4. Writing Sample Applicants must provide one writing sample of no more than 8,000 words . The writing sample should demonstrate the applicant s ability to conduct rigorous research and communicate academic arguments effectively. A strong writing sample should ideally showcase capabilities relevant to the fellowship, particularly qualitative research, social sciences, migration, ageing or a related area. How to Prepare a Strong Application Because this is a specialised postdoctoral research position, applicants should avoid submitting a generic academic application. Instead, the application should demonstrate a clear connection between the applicant s previous work and the project s research agenda. Highlight Relevant Research Experience Applicants should clearly explain any previous work involving: Migration Ageing Older adults Social networks Healthcare Eldercare Digital technologies Communities Integration Mobility Transnational relationships Demonstrate Fieldwork Experience If the applicant has previously conducted interviews, observations, ethnographic research, community research or other forms of qualitative fieldwork, these experiences should be clearly highlighted. Highlight Relevant Language Skills Applicants who have conversational proficiency in Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, Tagalog, Bahasa Indonesian or Vietnamese should clearly state this in their CV and cover letter. This is especially important because language capability is directly relevant to the proposed community-based fieldwork. Demonstrate Interdisciplinary Collaboration Applicants should provide examples of working with researchers, organisations or stakeholders from different professional or academic backgrounds. Strengthen the Publication Profile Where applicable, applicants should clearly list: Peer-reviewed journal publications Working papers Book chapters Conference presentations Research reports Other scholarly outputs The application should demonstrate the candidate s potential to build a strong publication record. Who Should Consider Applying? This opportunity is particularly suited to researchers who have recently completed, or are about to complete, a PhD and want to develop a research career focused on migration, ageing and related social issues. Potentially suitable candidates include researchers with backgrounds in: Social Geography Sociology Anthropology Migration Studies Social Sciences Humanities Related interdisciplinary fields Candidates should also have strong qualitative research capabilities and an interest in conducting fieldwork among foreign-born older adults in Singapore. title: Malmö University Paid PhD Positions 2026 in Sweden: Doctoral Jobs With Salary, No Tuition Fees and August Application Deadlines
summary: Malmö University in Sweden is currently advertising paid doctoral opportunities for 2026 , providing qualified graduates with the chance to pursue advanced research while holding an employed doctoral position at the university. For international graduates searching for paid PhD positions in Sweden, fully funded doctoral opportunities in Europe, PhD jobs with salary, or tuition-free doctoral studies in Sweden , Malmö University s current vacancies present several opportunities across different research areas. Unlike doctoral systems in which candidates primarily enrol as fee-paying students, a majority of doctoral students in Sweden are employed by their universities. Malmö University explains that candidates seeking admission to doctoral studies generally need to apply for and successfully obtain a vacant employed doctoral position . This employment arrangement is particularly significant because doctoral students can receive a salary, paid vacation leave and the right to paid parental leave while undertaking their doctoral research. Malmö University also states that students admitted to doctoral studies through the university do not pay admission or tuition fees . Several doctoral vacancies are currently listed by Malmö University, including opportunities in Organization Studies, International Migration and Ethnic Relations (IMER), and multi-omics research involving oral fluids and reproducible disease signatures . The application deadlines vary according to the individual position. Among the currently listed doctoral opportunities, deadlines include 14 August 2026 and 31 August 2026 . About Malmö University Doctoral Studies in Sweden Malmö University provides doctoral education for candidates who want to continue their academic and research careers beyond the master s level. A complete doctoral programme at Malmö University corresponds to four years of full-time study , equivalent to 240 higher education credits . Successful completion leads to a doctoral degree. The university also provides for an intermediate qualification. After completing two years of doctoral studies, corresponding to 120 higher education credits , a doctoral candidate can be awarded a licentiate degree . The overall structure is therefore: Four years of full-time doctoral study; 240 higher education credits for the complete programme; The possibility of a licentiate degree after 120 credits; and A doctoral degree following successful completion of the full doctoral programme. Doctoral education includes both research and coursework. In addition to completing a doctoral thesis, candidates undertake courses determined by the requirements of their doctoral subject and their individual study programme. Current Malmö University PhD Vacancies for 2026 Malmö University s current vacancies page confirms that doctoral positions are being advertised with specific closing dates. Applicants should understand that these are separate vacancies. Candidates need to review the individual advertisement for the position that matches their qualifications and research interests. 1. Doctoral Student in Organization Studies Malmö University is currently advertising employment as a doctoral student in Organization Studies . The vacancy is connected with the university s academic activities in Organization Studies and provides an opportunity for an eligible candidate to undertake doctoral-level research while employed as a doctoral student. Published: 4 June 2026 Application deadline: 14 August 2026 Applicants interested in this opportunity should consult the individual vacancy announcement for the complete research description, subject-specific eligibility requirements, requested application documents and selection criteria. 2. Doctoral Student in IMER With a Focus on Survey Studies of Diversity and Inclusion Another currently advertised opportunity is for a doctoral student in International Migration and Ethnic Relations (IMER) . The position has a particular focus on survey studies of diversity and inclusion . IMER is also one of Malmö University s listed doctoral subjects, making this vacancy relevant to graduates and researchers interested in areas connected with international migration, ethnic relations, diversity and inclusion. Published: 29 June 2026 Application deadline: 31 August 2026 Candidates should review the full vacancy announcement before applying because the individual advertisement may contain academic, methodological, language, research-experience and documentation requirements beyond Malmö University s general doctoral eligibility rules. 3. Doctoral Research Project in Multi-Omics of Oral Fluids and Disease Signatures Malmö University is also advertising a doctoral research project titled: “From Variability to Validation: Standardizing Multi-Omics of Oral Fluids for Reproducible Disease Signatures.” This doctoral opportunity is particularly relevant to candidates with an appropriate academic and research background for the scientific area addressed by the project. Published: 9 July 2026 Application deadline: 31 August 2026 Because this is a specialised doctoral research project, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the detailed academic and scientific requirements contained in the individual vacancy advertisement. Other Current Malmö University Vacancies In addition to the doctoral opportunities, Malmö University s vacancies page lists other academic and research employment opportunities. At the time represented by the supplied vacancy information, these include: Research Assistant in Trustworthy Machine Learning for Elderly Care; Associate Senior Lecturer in Applied Physics, oriented towards Machine Learning; Postdoctoral position in Criminology; and Hourly-paid Teaching Assistant in the IOIO Mechatronics Lab. These positions should not be confused with the doctoral vacancies because their employment levels, eligibility criteria, responsibilities and application requirements differ. Prospective PhD candidates should specifically identify vacancies described as doctoral student positions or doctoral research projects. Malmö University PhD Application Deadlines for 2026 There is no single university-wide application deadline for all doctoral studies at Malmö University. Each vacant doctoral position has its own application deadline. For the doctoral opportunities listed in the supplied 2026 vacancies information: Doctoral Student in Organization Studies — 14 August 2026 Doctoral Student in IMER, focusing on survey studies of diversity and inclusion — 31 August 2026 Doctoral Research Project on standardizing multi-omics of oral fluids for reproducible disease signatures — 31 August 2026 Applicants should not assume that one deadline applies to all Malmö University PhD opportunities. The deadline stated in the individual vacancy advertisement is the deadline that matters for that particular application. Paid PhD Employment at Malmö University A major feature of pursuing doctoral studies in Sweden is the employment structure available to doctoral candidates. Malmö University explains that a majority of doctoral students in Sweden are employed by their universities . This means that becoming a doctoral student can involve being both a researcher in training and a university employee. Malmö University specifically identifies important employment benefits associated with becoming a doctoral student, including: Salary; Paid vacation leave; and The right to paid parental leave. This makes Malmö University s employed doctoral vacancies particularly attractive to candidates looking for funded PhD opportunities in Europe. Applicants should consult each individual vacancy for the precise terms and conditions applying to that employment. No Admission or Tuition Fees for Doctoral Students Malmö University states that there are no admission or tuition fees for candidates admitted as doctoral students through the university. This is an important distinction for international applicants. Instead of paying tuition fees for the doctoral programme, successful candidates obtaining employed doctoral positions can receive a salary through their university employment. Candidates should nevertheless account for their individual circumstances and any expenses associated with relocation and living in Sweden. Alternative Financing Is Only Accepted in Special Circumstances Malmö University also addresses situations where doctoral studies would be financed through a route other than university employment. According to the university, alternative financing for doctoral studies where the doctoral candidate is not employed will only be accepted in special circumstances . Prospective applicants should therefore regard vacant employed doctoral positions as the principal route into doctoral studies at Malmö University rather than assuming that self-financing automatically provides an alternative route to admission. General Entry Requirements for Malmö University Doctoral Studies Applicants must satisfy the general entry requirements for third-cycle education. Malmö University refers to Chapter 7, Section 39 of the Swedish Higher Education Ordinance when explaining these requirements. A prospective doctoral candidate can meet the general entry requirements through several routes. Route 1: Second-Cycle Qualification A candidate can qualify if they have been awarded a second-cycle qualification . For many prospective applicants, particularly international graduates, this will mean possessing an appropriate postgraduate-level qualification corresponding to the required Swedish academic level. However, applicants must also examine the requirements of the particular doctoral position. Route 2: 240 Higher Education Credits Candidates can also satisfy the general requirement if they have completed courses comprising at least 240 credits , with at least 60 credits awarded at the second-cycle level . In summary: At least 240 higher education credits in total; and At least 60 higher education credits at second-cycle level. Route 3: Substantially Equivalent Knowledge Malmö University s eligibility information also recognizes candidates who have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or elsewhere . This provision is particularly relevant for international applicants whose qualifications may come from education systems that do not use the Swedish credit structure. Applicants should still allow the university to determine equivalence rather than assuming that a foreign qualification automatically satisfies a particular vacancy s requirements. Exemptions in Special Cases The university also notes that a higher education institution may permit an exemption from the general entry requirements for an individual applicant when there are special grounds . This should be viewed as an exceptional provision and not as the normal admissions pathway. General Requirements Are Not the Only Requirements Meeting the general doctoral entry requirements does not automatically make an applicant eligible for every doctoral vacancy at Malmö University . Each position may have additional requirements based on the research project and doctoral subject. Depending on the vacancy, these could concern an applicant s: Academic discipline; Previous degree; Master s-level studies; Research experience; Thesis or independent research work; Quantitative or qualitative research skills; Technical expertise; Methodological knowledge; Language abilities; or Other subject-specific competencies. Applicants must therefore read the complete vacancy advertisement for the doctoral position they want to pursue. Doctoral Subjects at Malmö University Malmö University offers doctoral education across a broad range of subjects. The university currently identifies the following doctoral subjects: Applied Physics ; Biomedical Science ; Care Science ; Computer Science ; Criminology ; Global Politics ; Health and Society Studies ; History and History Didactics ; Interaction Design ; International Migration and Ethnic Relations ; Language and Literature in Education ; Media and Communication Studies ; Odontology/Dentistry ; Organisation Studies ; Pedagogy ; Science Education and Mathematics Education ; Social Work ; Sport Science ; and Urban Studies . The breadth of these disciplines means prospective researchers from science, technology, healthcare, social sciences, education, migration studies, media, design and other academic backgrounds may find relevant doctoral opportunities when suitable vacancies become available. Doctoral courses In addition to the actual doctoral thesis, the doctoral study programme also includes one component course. The content of this course is governed by the general syllabus for the doctoral subject area. The specific courses that should be included in the study programme will be decided upon in consultation with the supervisors. Se current doctoral courses Doctoral Schools Doctoral schools bring together doctoral students with a common focus. That focus might be a postgraduate education subject or theme. The students conduct joint activities in the form of courses, workshops, and seminars. It is often the case that such schools are run in collaboration with other universities and financed with the help of external funding. International Applicants for Malmö University PhD Positions International candidates can consider Malmö University s doctoral vacancies. The university states that all international doctoral positions will be posted in English . Its general eligibility rules also recognize substantially equivalent knowledge acquired in Sweden or elsewhere . International candidates must nevertheless satisfy both: The general entry requirements for doctoral education; and The specific eligibility and selection requirements stated in the individual doctoral vacancy. Candidates should not interpret the international availability of a position as meaning that academic eligibility requirements are waived. How to Apply for Malmö University PhD Vacancies Malmö University s vacancies information provides important instructions about its recruitment system. Step 1: Find an Appropriate Vacancy Start by identifying an advertised doctoral position relevant to your academic background, research experience and interests. Do not simply select a position because it is labelled as a PhD opportunity. Carefully assess whether your qualifications correspond to the project s requirements. Step 2: Read the Complete Advertisement Open the individual vacancy and review: Academic requirements; Research area; Required qualifications; Selection criteria; Required supporting documents; Application instructions; and Application deadline. The vacancy advertisement should be treated as the authoritative source for position-specific requirements. Step 3: Create a User Account Malmö University states that applicants must have a user account to apply . Once you have found a position, you need to create an account or log into an existing account to continue with the application. Candidates applying directly through a vacancy advertisement can also be registered as new users. Step 4: Complete Your Applicant Profile The university identifies several benefits of maintaining a user account. These include: Pre-filled personal information when applying; A quick overview of submitted applications; and The ability to complete or change a submitted application before the deadline. Applicants should ensure that the information in their account remains accurate and update their details when necessary. Step 5: Upload the Required Documents Applications are assessed based on the qualifications and education registered in the application. Malmö University therefore advises applicants to complete their applications carefully and attach all required documents . Candidates should make sure their application provides sufficient evidence of the academic and professional qualifications relevant to the position. Step 6: Submit Before the Deadline Applicants must submit their application before the deadline specified for the vacancy. Where the system permits applicants to change or complete an application before the closing date, candidates should still avoid waiting until the final hours to submit. APPLY NOW How Applications Are Assessed Malmö University states that applications are selected based on the applicant s registered qualifications and education . This makes the accuracy and completeness of the application especially important. Applicants should carefully document their qualifications and provide the supporting documents required by the vacancy. A strong application should clearly allow assessors to determine how the candidate satisfies the advertised eligibility and selection criteria. Important Public-Document Notice for Applicants Prospective applicants should be aware of an important aspect of applying to a Swedish public university. Malmö University is a public authority . According to the university s recruitment information, members of the public may request access to official documents, including an applicant s application and other documents associated with the recruitment. Applicants should therefore understand that their submitted recruitment documents may be subject to public disclosure in accordance with applicable rules. Applicants With a Protected Identity Malmö University provides a separate application procedure for candidates with a protected identity. Such applicants are instructed to submit their application documents by post using a double envelope . The documents should be placed in an envelope marked “SEKRETESS” , which should be sealed and then placed inside a regular outer envelope. The application is sent to Malmö University s HR Department, with the relevant faculty or department identified. Applicants using this procedure are also instructed to contact the person or persons named in the vacancy advertisement so they know that the application documents are being sent by post. Candidates in this situation should follow Malmö University s current official instructions carefully. Doctoral Courses and Research Training Doctoral education at Malmö University goes beyond the doctoral thesis. The study programme also contains coursework governed by the general syllabus for the relevant doctoral subject. Specific courses to be incorporated into an individual doctoral programme are decided in consultation with supervisors. This enables the doctoral programme to combine: Independent research; Academic supervision; Subject-specific training; Research methodology; Relevant doctoral coursework; and Development toward the final doctoral thesis. Doctoral Schools and Academic Networking Malmö University also operates doctoral schools that bring together doctoral students around shared academic subjects or themes. Activities can include: Courses; Workshops; Seminars; and Other collaborative academic activities. Some doctoral schools are conducted in collaboration with other universities and can be supported through external funding. These structures can help doctoral candidates establish academic networks, engage with researchers beyond their immediate projects and participate in wider research communities. Visiting and Exchange Doctoral Students Malmö University also welcomes exchange doctoral students who want to conduct part of their research at the university within the framework of doctoral education undertaken elsewhere. Application procedures may vary between doctoral courses, so visiting or exchange doctoral candidates should check the instructions associated with the particular course or activity they want to pursue. Housing for Doctoral Students and Researchers Relocating to Sweden can be a major consideration for international applicants. Malmö University states that doctoral students, researchers and guest researchers can rent housing through the university . Candidates who successfully obtain a doctoral position should consult the university s current accommodation information to determine availability, conditions and the procedure for securing housing. Why Consider a Malmö University PhD Position? Several aspects make the current doctoral opportunities noteworthy. 1. Doctoral Students Can Be Salaried Employees The Swedish model means many doctoral students are university employees rather than solely students. 2. Paid Vacation Malmö University states that employed doctoral students receive paid vacation leave. 3. Paid Parental Leave Rights Doctoral employees also have the right to paid parental leave under the applicable employment arrangements. 4. No Doctoral Tuition Fees Malmö University states that there are no admission or tuition fees for candidates admitted as doctoral students through the university. 5. International Opportunities International doctoral positions are advertised in English, and the general eligibility framework recognizes substantially equivalent knowledge acquired outside Sweden. 6. Wide Range of Research Fields Malmö University offers doctoral education across 19 listed subjects, ranging from Applied Physics and Computer Science to Criminology, Global Politics, International Migration and Ethnic Relations, Social Work and Urban Studies. 7. Structured Research Environment Doctoral courses, supervision, workshops, seminars and doctoral schools provide opportunities for research training and academic networking. Important Dates for Applicants Candidates interested in the doctoral opportunities currently listed should pay close attention to the following deadlines: 14 August 2026: Application deadline for Employment as a Doctoral Student in Organization Studies. 31 August 2026: Application deadline for the Doctoral Student in IMER with a focus on survey studies of diversity and inclusion. 31 August 2026: Application deadline for the doctoral research project “From Variability to Validation: Standardizing Multi-Omics of Oral Fluids for Reproducible Disease Signatures.” These deadlines are position-specific. Applicants should verify the closing date and all other requirements in the individual vacancy announcement before submitting an application. Conclusion Malmö University s 2026 paid doctoral positions in Sweden provide an attractive opportunity for qualified graduates seeking advanced research training combined with university employment. A Malmö University doctoral programme normally corresponds to four years of full-time study and 240 higher education credits , ultimately leading to a doctoral degree. Anyone planning to apply should identify the doctoral vacancy that best matches their academic background, carefully study its position-specific eligibility requirements, create or log into the required applicant account, attach all requested documents and submit the application before the applicable deadline. title: IMETE 2026–2028 Applications Open: 6 Partial Scholarships for the International Master in Environmental Technology and Engineering
summary: Applications are still open for the International Master of Science in Environmental Technology and Engineering (IMETE) 2026–2028 intake , a two-year international master’s programme that allows students to study environmental engineering and water-related technologies across leading European institutions in the Czech Republic, the Netherlands and Belgium. For the 2026–2028 intake, six partial scholarships remain available , reducing the tuition fee to €3,000 for the entire two-year programme for eligible candidates. However, applicants should note an important change: there are no full Erasmus Mundus scholarships available for this intake . The remaining reduced-fee places are intended for self-funded candidates who either do not require a visa for Europe or are considered able to obtain the necessary visa sufficiently quickly. The programme states that candidates from countries where the visa process is expected to take too long will not be accepted for this intake because students must be able to begin their first semester in Prague on time. The final application deadline for the 2026–2028 intake is 31 August 2026 . About the International Master in Environmental Technology and Engineering The International Master in Environmental Technology and Engineering, commonly known as IMETE , is a multidisciplinary master’s programme focused on preparing a new generation of environmental engineers and scientists. The programme combines scientific knowledge, environmental engineering, practical experience and international mobility. Students study topics related to: Water treatment Wastewater treatment and reuse Desalination Environmental technologies Resource recovery Biological treatment processes Membrane technologies Environmental biotechnology Water-quality management Sustainable engineering The programme carries 120 ECTS credits , with students normally completing 30 ECTS per semester. Over two academic years, students study at several European universities and research institutions, gaining exposure to different academic environments, countries and approaches to environmental technology. IMETE 2026–2028 Programme Structure One of the defining characteristics of IMETE is its international mobility model. Students move between partner universities during different semesters. Semester 1: University of Chemistry and Technology, Prague The first semester takes place at the: University of Chemistry and Technology, Prague, Czech Republic Period: September to January Students begin building the scientific and engineering foundations needed for the remainder of the programme. Semester 2: IHE Delft Institute for Water Education The second semester takes place at: IHE Delft Institute for Water Education, Delft, the Netherlands Period: February to June IHE Delft has a strong focus on water-related education and research, making this semester particularly relevant for students developing expertise in environmental technology, wastewater management and water systems. Summer Internship During the first summer, while associated with IHE Delft, IMETE students normally undertake an internship lasting several weeks. Past student experiences described by the programme include placements involving: Air-treatment technologies Bioreactor systems Odour and gas-emission treatment Decentralised wastewater treatment Wastewater-treatment plant development Research and scientific writing Microbiological analysis Treatment-process optimisation These placements provide an opportunity to apply classroom knowledge to practical environmental-engineering challenges. Semester 3: Ghent University The third semester takes place at: Ghent University, Ghent, Belgium Period: September to January Students continue developing specialised knowledge while benefiting from another European research and academic environment. Semester 4: Master’s Dissertation The fourth and final semester runs approximately from: February to August/September Students complete their master’s dissertation at one of the three main consortium institutions or an associated IMETE partner. The dissertation carries 30 ECTS credits and forms an integrated part of the master’s programme. Potential Master’s Research Areas IMETE offers research possibilities across environmental engineering and water technologies. Desalination and Reuse Potential areas include: Seawater desalination Brackish-water desalination Membrane fouling Fouling prediction in reverse-osmosis systems Membrane scaling Performance prediction for membrane-based desalination Membrane-cleaning optimisation Pretreatment for desalination Post-treatment of desalinated water Biological fouling prevention Reducing chemical use Reducing energy consumption Minimising environmental impacts Wastewater reuse for ultra-pure water Wastewater Treatment and Reuse Potential topics include: Domestic wastewater treatment Agricultural wastewater reuse Emerging contaminants Decentralised wastewater infrastructure Nitrogen conversion Industrial wastewater management Resource recovery Biomass valorisation Environmental DNA Microbial-source tracking Water-quality analysis Bioreactors Photo-activated sludge Granular treatment processes Biochar-based filters Hydrothermal sludge treatment The range of research areas makes the programme relevant to students interested in both fundamental scientific research and applied environmental engineering. What Makes the IMETE Programme Attractive? High-Quality Environmental Engineering Education The programme introduces students to contemporary technologies in: Water treatment Wastewater treatment Desalination Water reuse Environmental engineering Students learn within universities and institutes that have established expertise in environmental and water-related research. International Exposure IMETE is inherently international. Students study in at least three European countries and interact with classmates, faculty members and researchers from different cultural and professional backgrounds. The mobility structure provides exposure to several academic systems and approaches to environmental challenges. Hands-On Experience The programme combines academic study with practical experience. Internships, laboratory activities, research projects and the master’s dissertation allow participants to apply theoretical knowledge to real environmental and engineering problems. Students may also receive guidance from international mentors and supervisors with specialised expertise. Admission Requirements Applicants must satisfy several academic requirements. Academic Degree Candidates should have successfully completed a first higher-education degree equivalent to a Bachelor of Science degree of approximately 180 ECTS . Applicants who have not yet completed their bachelor’s degree may still apply if they have successfully completed at least 120 ECTS . If admitted conditionally, they must obtain the first degree no later than 15 August 2026 . Academic Performance Applicants should normally demonstrate a good academic record equivalent to approximately: GPA of at least B/B+ under the U.S. system, or At least a UK upper-second-class equivalent Relevant Academic Background Acceptable backgrounds include pure or applied sciences such as: Chemistry Biology Geology Civil engineering Agricultural engineering Environmental sciences Agricultural sciences Other closely related scientific or engineering disciplines Scientific Preparation Applicants must have sufficient academic knowledge of: Mathematics Physics Chemistry Basic knowledge of biology is recommended. English Language Requirements Applicants normally need to provide evidence from an internationally recognised English-language test. Some nationalities may be exempt according to the programme’s English-language rules. However, candidates from countries where English is used as the language of university instruction but which are not included on the official exemption list must still provide an accepted English-language test result. A university letter stating that previous education was conducted in English will not replace the required test in such cases. Applicants may submit their main application before receiving the test result. The final deadline for uploading the required English-language test is: 31 August 2026 Required Application Documents Applicants should prepare the following documentation. 1. Academic Diploma A copy of the applicant’s degree certificate is required. Where necessary, documents should be accompanied by an English translation prepared by a sworn translator. 2. Certified Academic Transcripts Applicants should provide certified transcripts or mark sheets. If the grading system is not explained clearly on the transcript, documentation explaining the official grading system should also be provided. 3. Curriculum Vitae The CV should include relevant: Education Employment Professional experience Research experience, where applicable 4. Motivation Questions Applicants will need to answer several questions through the online application. These address topics such as: Why the applicant wants to join IMETE Environmental challenges the applicant wants to address How the programme will help address those challenges Relevant qualifications and experience The applicant’s five-year career vision 5. Two Recommendation Letters Applicants need two letters of recommendation , preferably issued within the previous six months. They may come from: Two university teachers, or One university teacher and one employer, or Internationally recognised scientists The letters should address the applicant’s academic, scientific, professional and personal potential. They should be dated, signed and issued on official letterhead. 6. English-Language Test An accepted English-language test result must be submitted unless the applicant qualifies for an official exemption. Application documents must generally be uploaded as PDF files, with a maximum file size of 2 MB per file. Six Reduced-Tuition Scholarships Available For the 2026–2028 intake , the programme states that approximately six partial scholarships remain available . Successful recipients pay: €3,000 total tuition for the entire two-year programme This is a significant reduction compared with the stated external-sponsor tuition fee. However, candidates should understand that this is not a fully funded scholarship . There are no full Erasmus Mundus scholarships available for the 2026–2028 intake . Financial Responsibilities Students receiving the reduced tuition rate must be capable of financing the remaining costs themselves or through other funding. Tuition For eligible self-paying students under the reduced-fee arrangement: €3,000 for the full two-year programme For candidates funded by an external sponsor, the stated tuition fee is: €22,500 for two years Insurance Approximately: €34 per month , or roughly €835 for 24.5 months Visa and Residence Permits Where required, visa and residence-permit expenses are estimated at approximately: €1,000 Living and Travel Costs Students are advised to budget at least: €1,220 per month This amount is intended to cover living expenses and travel between partner institutions. Candidates must demonstrate that they have sufficient financial resources to cover tuition, insurance and living costs. Financial confirmation is required no later than 31 August 2026 . Visa Requirement for the 2026–2028 Intake The visa condition deserves particular attention. The programme states that the remaining 2026–2028 reduced-fee opportunities are intended for candidates who: Do not require a visa for Europe, or Can obtain the necessary visa relatively easily and quickly Due to lengthy visa procedures for the Czech Republic, applicants who require a visa are strongly advised to begin arrangements as early as possible. The programme states that it will not accept students from countries where the visa procedure would take too long for timely enrolment. Applicants should therefore confirm their individual visa circumstances before investing substantial time in the application. Rent Benefit in the Netherlands Students studying at IHE Delft may potentially qualify for the Dutch rent benefit system. Much of IHE Delft’s student accommodation is reportedly eligible. Students who meet the relevant requirements can apply through the Dutch tax authorities and may receive financial assistance covering a portion of their rent. Eligibility is determined by Dutch authorities and should not be treated as guaranteed programme funding. Post-Graduation Job-Seeking Opportunities IMETE graduates may also have opportunities to remain temporarily in participating countries after completing the degree to look for employment. According to the programme information, graduates may potentially stay: Up to one year in the Netherlands Up to one year in Belgium Up to nine months in the Czech Republic These possibilities generally relate to orientation-year or job-seeking residence permits and remain subject to national immigration rules. Application Deadline The final deadline for the 2026–2028 intake is: 31 August 2026 The same date applies to several important requirements, including: Final programme application English-language test submission Financial confirmation Scholarship/reduced-fee outcomes are expected to be communicated following selection in early September 2026 . Because the first semester takes place in Prague and Czech visa processing may be lengthy, applicants requiring immigration permission should not wait until the final deadline. title: 3 U.S. Federal SBIR/STTR Funding Opportunities 2026: NIH, NSF and Defense Grants for Small Businesses
summary: Three major federal funding windows are available in 2026 for U.S. startups and small businesses developing technologies in health, deep tech, national security and other research-intensive sectors. The opportunities come from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) , the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) and the U.S. Department of Defense Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer ecosystem , including opportunities administered through components such as the Defense Logistics Agency. Together, these programmes provide non-dilutive federal research and development funding that can help small companies establish technical feasibility, develop prototypes, advance research toward commercialization and build partnerships with universities or nonprofit research institutions. Founders should pay particular attention to the upcoming 2026 deadlines because each programme operates under different submission rules, eligibility requirements and funding phases. 1. NIH Small Business Technology Transfer Grant: Parent STTR R41/R42 The NIH Small Business Technology Transfer Grant, Parent STTR [R41/R42], Clinical Trial Optional , is designed to support U.S. small businesses conducting biomedical or life-sciences research and development in partnership with nonprofit research institutions. The funding opportunity is listed as PA-27-102 and is part of the federal STTR programme, also commonly associated with America’s Seed Fund. About the NIH STTR Programme NIH uses the SBIR and STTR programmes to help U.S.-owned and operated small businesses develop technologies and products that support its mission to improve health, extend life and reduce illness and disability. STTR differs from SBIR because projects funded through STTR must include a formal collaboration with a nonprofit research institution, such as a university. The Principal Investigator may be employed by either the small business or the collaborating nonprofit research institution. However, the funding award itself is made to the eligible small business. Businesses whose projects do not require this type of institutional collaboration may instead consider the NIH SBIR funding route. What the NIH STTR Funding Supports The programme supports research and development required to move an innovative idea toward a commercially viable product. Eligible applications may fall under several funding stages: Phase I: Establishes technical merit and feasibility. Phase II: Continues research and development toward commercialization. Direct to Phase II: Available through NIH for businesses that have already demonstrated feasibility without previously receiving a Phase I award for the project. Fast-Track: Allows Phase I and Phase II to be submitted and reviewed together. After Phase II, NIH generally expects companies to continue commercialization using non-SBIR/STTR funding. Research Scope Proposals should contribute to the missions of participating NIH, CDC or FDA components. Relevant projects may span biomedical technologies, health technologies, diagnostics, life sciences, medical research and other areas aligned with participating institutes and centres. Applicants are encouraged to contact the appropriate NIH Institute, Center or Office before submission to determine whether their project is a suitable fit. Clinical trials may be included under the Parent STTR opportunity, but some participating NIH Institutes and Centers do not accept clinical-trial applications through this specific funding announcement. Applicants proposing clinical research should therefore carefully review component-specific rules. NIH Application Timeline The funding opportunity was released on 28 May 2026 and opened on 5 August 2026 . The solicitation lists standard due dates of: 5 September 2026 5 January 2027 5 April 2027 The provided funding summary notes that the September 2026 submission deadline is effectively 8 September 2026 , because 5 September falls on a Saturday and the following Monday is Labor Day. Applicants should verify the operative deadline through the official agency solicitation before submission. APPLY HERE 2. NSF SBIR/STTR Phase I, Phase II and Fast-Track Programmes The second opportunity is the NSF 26-510 Small Business Innovation Research / Small Business Technology Transfer Phase I, Phase II and Fast-Track Programs , administered through the U.S. National Science Foundation’s Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships. The programme supports startups and small businesses developing high-risk technologies with strong potential for commercial impact. What NSF SBIR/STTR Supports NSF describes the programme as a mechanism for transforming scientific discoveries and technological breakthroughs into products and services. Funding can support technologies across a broad range of areas, potentially including: Artificial intelligence Robotics Semiconductors Biotechnology Medical devices Advanced manufacturing Quantum technologies Clean energy Data technologies Computing Other emerging and deep-technology sectors NSF does not generally procure specific products through this programme. Instead, it invests in the research and development needed to turn promising technologies into commercially viable innovations. NSF takes no equity in funded businesses, and awardees retain ownership of their companies and intellectual property. NSF Phase I Funding Phase I supports technical research and development at an early stage. Businesses may request up to: $305,000 Projects generally run for approximately 6 to 18 months . Phase I is designed to reduce technical risk and establish whether a technology has sufficient merit and feasibility to justify continued development. NSF Phase II Funding Phase II supports companies that have successfully completed an eligible NSF Phase I award. Funding may reach: $1,250,000 Phase II projects typically run for approximately 24 months and focus on advancing technical development and commercialization. Only eligible NSF Phase I awardees may submit Phase II proposals. NSF Fast-Track Funding The Fast-Track programme combines Phase I and Phase II development. Funding may reach approximately: $1,555,000 The Phase I portion may include up to $400,000, followed by up to approximately $1.155 million for the Phase II component. Additional NSF Funding Pathways Existing Phase II awardees may also have access to: Phase IIB supplements Technology Enhancement for Commercial Partnerships supplements Strategic Breakthrough opportunities Strategic Breakthrough proposals may, following invitation or consultation with the relevant NSF Programme Officer, request substantially larger amounts for exceptional technologies approaching commercial readiness. Project Pitch Requirement A major requirement applies to new Phase I and Fast-Track applicants. Before submitting a full proposal, companies must submit an official Project Pitch and receive an invitation from NSF. For Phase I, the invitation generally remains valid for the next two eligible submission deadlines. For Fast-Track, the full proposal must be submitted within four months of receiving the invitation. NSF limits the number of Project Pitches that a company can submit. NSF Eligibility Applicants must qualify as U.S. small business concerns. The programme generally applies to firms with no more than 500 employees, including affiliates . For STTR proposals, the business must also partner with a research institution. The Principal Investigator must be primarily employed by the small business, generally meaning at least 51% employment with the company. The PI must also have the legal right to work for the company in the United States. NSF does not impose a specific degree requirement on the PI. NSF Review Criteria Proposals are evaluated according to three major criteria: Intellectual Merit Broader Impacts Commercial Potential Strong proposals should therefore demonstrate not only interesting science or engineering, but also a realistic pathway from research to meaningful commercial use. NSF Deadline The next major full-proposal deadline is: 4 November 2026 at 5:00 p.m. in the submitting organisation’s local time Additional scheduled deadlines include March and July 2027. APPLY HERE 3. Department of Defense SBIR/STTR 2026 Release Cycle The third opportunity comes through the U.S. Department of Defense SBIR/STTR system. Participating defense components may release research topics addressing technological needs across areas such as: National security Autonomy Space technologies Cybersecurity Advanced materials Supply-chain technologies Logistics Manufacturing Defense systems Other mission-related technologies The Defense Logistics Agency is one participating organisation within the broader defense innovation ecosystem. About Defense SBIR/STTR Programmes The SBIR programme supports research and development conducted by qualifying small businesses, while STTR supports cooperative R D involving small companies and nonprofit U.S. research institutions. The programmes generally follow three phases: Phase I: Demonstrate technical feasibility. Phase II: Develop prototypes, processes or products for proof-of-concept. Phase III: Commercial application of the technology using funding outside the SBIR/STTR set-aside. The broader objective is to stimulate innovation, advance commercialization and develop technologies relevant to defense needs. 2026 Release Schedule The provided 2026 schedule includes multiple monthly-style release cycles. For Release 5 : Pre-release: 5 August 2026 Opens: 26 August 2026 Closes: 23 September 2026 Evaluation period through: 22 December 2026 Expected awards: 22 March 2027 For Release 6 : Pre-release: 2 September 2026 Opens: 23 September 2026 Closes: 21 October 2026 Dates are subject to change. Companies should monitor the Defense SBIR/STTR Innovation Portal for individual topics because technical requirements, participating components and eligibility details can vary by solicitation. Training and Compliance Companies participating in certain Defense Logistics Agency innovation programmes should also be aware of compliance and training requirements. These may include: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification training Controlled Unclassified Information training Enhanced Joint Certification Program requirements Foreign Ownership, Control and Influence training Applicants should review the requirements attached to the specific topic before preparing a proposal. APPLY HERE Key Deadlines to Remember For founders considering these three opportunities, the immediate dates are: NIH STTR: September 2026 cycle; the provided summary identifies 8 September 2026 as the adjusted deadline Defense SBIR/STTR Release 5: 23 September 2026 NSF SBIR/STTR: 4 November 2026 at 5:00 p.m. local time Because some programmes require preliminary steps, founders should not treat the full-proposal deadline as the date to begin preparing. NSF Phase I and Fast-Track applicants, for example, must obtain a Project Pitch invitation before submitting the complete proposal. Conclusion The NIH, NSF and Department of Defense SBIR/STTR programmes provide three substantial pathways for U.S. small businesses seeking non-dilutive research and development funding in 2026. NIH may be particularly relevant to biomedical and health-focused companies collaborating with research institutions. NSF offers broad support for high-risk deep technologies with commercial potential, including funding of up to $305,000 for Phase I and $1.25 million for Phase II. Defense SBIR/STTR opportunities provide recurring topic-based windows for companies developing technologies relevant to national security and defense needs. Founders should identify the programme that best matches their technology, confirm their eligibility and begin preparing well before the deadline. Federal innovation funding can be generous, but it rewards preparation; bureaucracy rarely becomes more charming when met at 4:57 p.m. To discover more grant opportunities, CLICK HERE .
